answer: One-person credentials. Before rewarding falcon image labels, basalt measurements, or quill manuscript transcriptions, require a credential from an issuer that checks each human once. A zero-knowledge proof exposes one epoch-specific nullifier; duplicate nullifiers receive no extra reward across accounts. An attacker seeking N quotas must recruit N enrolled people and pay their cooperation costs. This depends on reliable deduplication and credentials that cannot be cheaply sold or stolen; colluding humans remain a bypass.
